title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as new contracts, funding rounds, and international agreements reshape the landscape. Notable movements include Rocket Lab's expansion plans and the U.S. bolstering its space resilience budget.

themes.title: International Agreements Heat Up
themes.body: Paraguay's signing of the Artemis Accords marks another step in the global push for lunar cooperation. This move could signal a shift in how smaller nations engage with major space powers.

themes.title: Funding and Acquisitions on the Rise
themes.body: Rocket Lab's large launch contract and acquisition plans highlight a trend of consolidation and investment in space robotics. Meanwhile, Lunar Outpost's $30 million raise suggests a growing appetite for lunar infrastructure.

themes.title: Defense and Space Convergence
themes.body: The collaboration between Anduril and L3Harris on a tactical SDA constellation illustrates the increasing overlap between defense tech and space capabilities. As the Pentagon seeks to enhance its space posture, expect more such partnerships.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hiccups Persist
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests raise questions about the pace of U.S. advancements in this critical area. With three consecutive quarters of setbacks, the pressure is on to deliver results.
